name: B10-0233/2024 (PPE) – 11th year of the occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol by the Russian Federation and the deteriorating human rights situation in occupied Crimea, notably the cases of Iryna Danylovych, Tofik Abdul
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the 11th year of the occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol by the Russian Federation and the deteriorating human rights situation in occupied Crimea, notably the cases of Iryna Danylovych, Tofik Abdulhaziiev and Amet Suleymanov
part_text:
The European Parliament calls on Russia to end its occupation of Crimea, which began in 2014, and to withdraw its military forces from all of Ukraine. It demands the release of three jailed Ukrainians: journalist Iryna Danylovych, activist Tofik Abdulhaziiev and citizen journalist Amet Suleymanov. It also asks other countries to keep refusing to recognise Russia's annexation of Crimea, to investigate human rights abuses there since 2014, and to add sanctions on people and organisations involved. This is the Parliament's opinion; it does not itself change any law.

- Russia is asked to leave Crimea and free three named prisoners; no law changes.
- The call targets Russia, other countries and international bodies, not EU citizens directly.
- The Parliament sends its demand to EU leaders, member states, Ukraine and Russia.
